pool.text: The 5th Dalai Lama unified Tibet and moved administration to the city.
Reconstruction of the famous Potala Palace began on the Red Hill.
The Potrang Karpo or White Palace of the Potala was completed.
The armies of the Qing dynasty entered the city and sent resident commissioners.
The Qing Emperor reorganized the Tibetan government and set up the Kashag council.
A British expedition captured and briefly occupied the city in January.
All remaining Chinese troops left the city after the Xinhai turmoil.
The Chinese People's Liberation Army launched the Battle of Chamdo.
Following a failed uprising, the 14th Dalai Lama and associates fled Tibet.
Lhasa City was established as a formal administrative entity in January.
Lhasa Gonggar International Airport was built as the aviation hub of Tibet.
The Tibet Autonomous Region was established with the city as its capital.
The Lhasa Brewery Company was established on the northern outskirts of the city.
The Potala Palace was officially inscribed to the UNESCO World Heritage List.
The Tibet Museum was inaugurated as the official regional museum.
The Monument to the Peaceful Liberation of Tibet was unveiled in Potala Square.
The city has been served by rail since the Qinghai–Tibet Railway opened.
The Lhasa Airport Expressway was completed, reducing travel time to the airport.
The city was connected to Shigatse by a new rail service.
Construction began on the Sichuan–Tibet railway linking the city to Nyingchi County.
